fields.Name: Schema Documentation Sweep
fields.Description: Finds MemberJunction entity fields that have no description and proposes one for each, then asks a person to approve them. A workflow demo that runs entirely on framework metadata — every install has undocumented fields, so it has real work to do on day one without any business data. The approval step is a genuine human-in-the-loop pause: the graph waits, every other branch keeps running, and answering releases it.

fields.Name: Find undocumented fields
fields.Description: Reads MJ: Entity Fields for rows with no Description. Capped low on purpose — this is a demo, and a sweep of every undocumented field in a stock install would be thousands of prompt calls.

fields.DestinationStepID: @lookup:MJ: AI Agent Steps.Name=Propose a description for each field&AgentID=@parent:AgentID
fields.Description: Feeds the records into the loop. Without this edge the two steps are disconnected and only the starting step is ever compiled — the workflow silently does half its job.

fields.Name: Propose a description for each field
fields.Description: One prompt call per field. A Prompt step rather than a sub-agent because there is nothing to reason about across turns — it is a single transformation of one field into one sentence, and an agent wrapper would add a reasoning loop, guardrails and a run record for no benefit.
fields.PromptID: @lookup:MJ: AI Prompts.Name=Workflow Demo: Propose Field Description

fields.DestinationStepID: @lookup:MJ: AI Agent Steps.Name=Approve the proposed descriptions&AgentID=@parent:AgentID
fields.Description: Proposals go to a person before anything is written.

fields.Name: Approve the proposed descriptions
fields.Description: Review the proposed field descriptions and approve the ones worth keeping. Each carries a confidence rating; treat anything marked low as a guess that needs checking against the field's real use.

fields.Name: Content Pipeline
fields.Description: Researches a topic from two angles, drafts a short piece, and revises it against brand rules until it passes or gives up. A workflow demo of the three graph shapes a linear flow cannot express: an AND-join, a bounded While loop, and an exclusive pair where exactly one branch runs.

fields.Name: Research: broad
fields.Description: One half of the research join. Runs in parallel with the focused search — they are independent, so making them sequential would double the wait for no reason.

ActionInputMapping.SearchTerms: what is a directed acyclic graph used for in workflow automation

fields.Description: Half of the AND-join into the draft step.
Reaches the second research angle. Both still feed the draft, so the join below still waits for BOTH.

fields.Name: Research: focused
fields.Description: The other half of the research join, reached from the broad search. NOT a second starting step: a workflow has exactly one entry, and a step marked as a second one is pruned as unreachable — which is how this demo spent its early life drafting from half the evidence.

ActionInputMapping.SearchTerms: task graph dispatcher durable execution retry semantics

fields.Description: The other half of the AND-join. The draft waits for BOTH.

fields.Name: Draft the piece
fields.Description: The AND-join. Two paths lead here, so the dispatcher holds this step until both research steps have settled — that is what a graph gives you that a linear flow cannot.

fields.DestinationStepID: @lookup:MJ: AI Agent Steps.Name=Review against brand rules&AgentID=@parent:AgentID
fields.Description: Every draft is reviewed, however good it looks.

fields.Name: Review against brand rules
fields.Description: A bounded While loop. Its body reviews AND revises in ONE iteration, because a task graph is acyclic and check-then-revise-then-check-again is not drawable. The loop runs again only to re-check the revision, and gives up after three attempts rather than spending forever on a draft that is not converging.
The winning branch when the draft passed. Higher priority so it is chosen when both conditions could be read as true.

fields.DestinationStepID: @lookup:MJ: AI Agent Steps.Name=Close out: gave up&AgentID=@parent:AgentID
fields.Description: The give-up branch. The loop hit its cap without the draft passing, and that has to be SAID — a workflow that gives up quietly is indistinguishable from one that succeeded.

fields.Name: Close out: approved
fields.Description: One of an exclusive pair — exactly one of these two runs, and the other settles Skipped, which is a normal outcome and never rendered as a failure.

fields.Name: Close out: gave up
fields.Description: The other half of the exclusive pair. Sets needsHuman so the stalled work is findable — the whole point of a give-up branch is that someone learns about it.
